license_notice: Original chord-only educational studies of common jazz forms; standards named as related repertoire are not exact/authorized lead sheets. No copyrighted melodies, lyrics, or backing recordings are bundled.

exercises.title: Hear the Form
exercises.instructions: Clap once at the start of each 4-bar phrase while listening or counting. Name the beginning of each 12-bar chorus.

exercises.title: Swing on Two and Four
exercises.instructions: Set metronome clicks on beats 2 and 4. Clap or play quarter notes, then swing eighths without rushing.

exercises.title: F Blues Scale Vocabulary
exercises.instructions: Play F, Ab, Bb, B, C, Eb, F slowly. Make two-bar questions and answers using only these notes.

exercises.title: Sing the Roots
exercises.instructions: Look at the progression; sing the root of each new chord before playing it. Repeat without looking.

exercises.title: Guide Tones Through ii–V–I
exercises.instructions: Over Dm7 → G7 → Cmaj7, play each third and seventh. Move each voice by the smallest distance possible.

exercises.title: Seventh-Chord Arpeggio Paths
exercises.instructions: Play 1–3–5–7 and back for m7, dominant 7, and maj7 chords. Connect to the nearest tone of the next chord.

exercises.title: Solo Using Only Chord Tones
exercises.instructions: Improvise one 12-bar chorus using only chord roots, thirds, fifths, and sevenths. End phrases with space.

exercises.title: Two-Bar Call and Response
exercises.instructions: Play a short two-bar phrase, leave two beats of silence, then answer with a related two-bar phrase.
exercises.suggested_material: F blues, no melody recording required

exercises.title: Count a 12-Bar Blues
exercises.instructions: Count measures 1–12 aloud while clapping beat 2 and 4. Identify IV at measure 5 and the turnaround at measures 11–12.

exercises.title: Rootless Guide-Tone Shells
exercises.instructions: On piano or guitar, voice just 3rd and 7th of each ii–V–I chord. Keep movement minimal; bass can play roots separately.

exercises.title: Motif and Rhythmic Variation
exercises.instructions: Improvise a two-bar motif, then repeat it with a changed rhythm, preserving one recognizable interval or accent.

exercises.title: Transcribe a Four-Bar Phrase
exercises.instructions: Listen to an authorized recording. Sing a four-bar phrase, locate pitches slowly, then reproduce the rhythm without sheet music.
exercises.suggested_material: Bring your own licensed audio; no default recording

exercises.title: Walking Bass: Roots and Approach Tones
exercises.instructions: Play one quarter note per beat. Start with chord roots on beat 1 and approach the next root by step or chromatic neighbor.

exercises.title: Comping with Space
exercises.instructions: Play sparse 2–4 note voicings with clear rests. Avoid constant quarter-note attacks; listen for where a soloist could breathe.

exercises.title: Build a One-Chorus Solo
exercises.instructions: Chorus 1: rhythmic motif. Chorus 2: guide-tone targets. Chorus 3: combine, leaving at least one full bar of rest. Record a note afterward.

exercises.title: Learn a Short Original Melody by Ear
exercises.instructions: Listen to a user-provided or original four-bar phrase; sing it before playing, then repeat it in two keys.

exercises.title: Listen to the Bass Line
exercises.instructions: During a licensed recording, focus only on bass. Hum the roots and note where the line approaches the next chord.

exercises.title: Three Minutes of Musical Play
exercises.instructions: Explore a phrase, groove, or voicing that interests you. No scoring or right answer; end by noting one discovery.

exercises.title: B♭ Blues: Say the Changes
exercises.instructions: Count three 4-bar phrases while naming each chord’s root. Play the third of each dominant seventh chord, then improvise one two-bar phrase.

exercises.title: Rhythm Changes: Hear the Bridge
exercises.instructions: Play the A-section progression once, then isolate bars 17–24. Follow D7 → G7 → C7 → F7 roots and return to the A section.

exercises.title: Minor Bossa: Guide Tones
exercises.instructions: Play thirds and sevenths of each chord in a relaxed straight-eighth-note feel. Loop bars 9–12 before playing all 16 bars.
exercises.suggested_material: Minor Bossa in C Minor (16-bar Study)

exercises.title: Relative Major to Minor
exercises.instructions: Play roots then guide tones through the 8-bar cycle. Identify the move from G major to E minor, keeping time at a slow swing tempo.

exercises.title: Modal Motif: Leave Space
exercises.instructions: Create a two-note motif in D Dorian. Repeat it with rhythmic variation and adapt the motif when the harmony shifts up a semitone.
exercises.suggested_material: Two-Center Modal Study in D (16 bars)

exercises.title: Recognize ABAC Form
exercises.instructions: Mark the end of each 8-bar section. Compare bars 9–16 and 25–32, then improvise one chorus using only chord tones.

exercises.title: AABA: Track the Bridge
exercises.instructions: Count the four 8-bar sections out loud. In the bridge, play chord roots on beat 1 and seventh-to-third voice leading without stopping.

exercises.title: Minor Blues in Three Phrases
exercises.instructions: Play a chorus with the minor pentatonic scale, then one with only chord tones. Note where bars 9–10 increase harmonic tension.

exercises.title: Slow Ballad: Smooth Voice Leading
exercises.instructions: Keep the tempo slow. Play only third and seventh notes with minimal motion, leaving a beat of silence after each chord change.

paths.title: Your First Week of Jazz
paths.guidance: Seven suggested sessions, not consecutive-day requirements. Repeat any day. Short sessions count.

paths.title: Learn a Tune by Ear
paths.guidance: Use an original or rights-cleared tune. Hear → sing → changes → voice-lead → improvise.

paths.title: Better Swing and Time Feel
paths.guidance: Alternate 2-and-4 metronome, no-click phrases and playing with a band.
